claims.source: To The Stars Academy of Arts and Science Inc., Form 1-K Part II, SEC EDGAR, filed April 2018
claims.text: As of April 2018 TTSA had raised approximately $1.09 million under a Regulation A offering that targeted up to $50 million; FY2017 net loss was $30,665,436, driven by $29,535,799 of stock-based compensation.

TTSA's SEC filing covering the period to June 2018 showed a $37.4 million accumulated deficit and $129,000 cash, with auditors flagging doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern.

label: Thomas Matthew DeLonge
narrative: DeLonge is the improbable assembly point. A rock musician with no clearance and no government service, he spent 2015-2017 courting serving and retired intelligence and aerospace officials, and in October 2017 he put six of them on a single masthead. To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. was incorporated in Delaware as a public benefit corporation with DeLonge as President and, per the 2017 Form 1-K, interim Chief Executive Officer; his family entity Gravity Holdings LLC held 60,000,000 of the 70,000,000 Class A shares. He is the reason a former Skunk Works program director, a retired CIA Senior Intelligence Service officer, the physicist behind the CIA remote-viewing program, a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, and the man who had just resigned from OUSD(I) all appeared in the same SEC filing. He signed TTSA to the History Channel for 'Unidentified: Inside America's UFO Investigation' as executive producer, and the company he built was the vehicle that first hosted the FLIR1, Gimbal and GoFast videos publicly. He is also the reason the effort carries a permanent credibility tax: TTSA's Regulation A+ raise sold roughly $1 million of a $50 million target while carrying a $37.4 million accumulated deficit, and by 2022 the entity had renamed itself To The Stars Inc. and returned to entertainment.
